text: The secret of getting ahead is getting started.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Kindness is the language which the deaf can hear and the blind can see.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The reports of my death are greatly exaggerated.
source: Telegram to the Associated Press, 1897 (wording commonly modernized)

text: Whenever you find yourself on the side of the majority, it is time to reform (or pause and reflect).
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source wording varies

text: A lie can travel halfway around the world while the truth is putting on its shoes.
source: Frequently attributed to Twain; attribution uncertain

text: If you tell the truth, you don't have to remember anything.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Good friends, good books, and a sleepy conscience: this is the ideal life.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The human race has one really effective weapon, and that is laughter.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The best way to cheer yourself up is to try to cheer somebody else up.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Age is an issue of mind over matter. If you don't mind, it doesn't matter.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Courage is resistance to fear, mastery of fear—not absence of fear.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The man who does not read has no advantage over the man who cannot read.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Never put off until tomorrow what you can do the day after tomorrow just as well.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: I have never let my schooling interfere with my education.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The human mind is a wonderful thing. It starts working the moment you are born and never stops until you stand up to speak in public.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; wording varies

text: Wrinkles should merely indicate where smiles have been.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: A classic is something that everybody wants to have read and nobody wants to read.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The difference between the almost right word and the right word is the difference between lightning and a lightning bug.
source: Letter to George Bainton, 1888

text: Truth is stranger than fiction, but it is because fiction is obliged to stick to possibilities; truth isn't.
source: Following the Equator, 1897

text: The lack of money is the root of all evil.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: A man who carries a cat by the tail learns something he can learn in no other way.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The more I learn about people, the more I like my dog.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: A man cannot be comfortable without his own approval.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: It is better to keep your mouth closed and let people think you are a fool than to open it and remove all doubt.
source: Commonly attributed to Twain; source uncertain

text: A banker is a fellow who lends you his umbrella when the sun shines and wants it back the minute it begins to rain.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: I can live for two months on a good compliment.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Never argue with stupid people; they will drag you down to their level and then beat you with experience.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: When angry, count four; when very angry, swear.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The finest clothing is a person's skin, but, of course, society demands something more than this.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Don't part with your illusions. When they are gone you may still exist, but you have ceased to live.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The two most important days in your life are the day you are born and the day you find out why.
source: Often attributed to Twain; attribution uncertain

text: A person with a new idea is a crank until the idea succeeds.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: There is no sadder thing than a young pessimist, except an old optimist.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The worst loneliness is not to be comfortable with yourself.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Thunder is good, thunder is impressive; but it is lightning that does the work.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: A man's character may be learned from the adjectives which he habitually uses in conversation.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Don't let schooling interfere with your education.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; wording variant

text: A good marriage is one where each partner secretly suspects they got the better deal.
source: Attributed to Twain; source uncertain

text: I do not like work, even when somebody else does it.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Familiarity breeds contempt—and children.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The easy confidence with which I know another man's religion is folly teaches me to suspect that mine is also.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Man is the only animal that blushes—or needs to.
source: Following the Equator, 1897 (wording variant)

text: The very ink with which history is written is merely fluid prejudice.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: I have been complimented many times, and I have always been embarrassed; I have always felt that they could have said more.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The fear of death follows from the fear of life. A man who lives fully is prepared to die at any time.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: There are lies, damned lies, and statistics.
source: Popularly attributed to Twain; attribution disputed

text: The human being is the only animal that can make a bargain—and the only one that needs to.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: I was gratified to be able to answer promptly, and I did. I said I didn't know.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: The trouble is not in dying for a friend, but in finding a friend worth dying for.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain

text: Suppose you were an idiot, and suppose you were a member of Congress; but I repeat myself.
source: Attributed to Mark Twain; source uncertain
